column4: The School of Failure: A Story About Success
column8: Books > Children's Books > Growing Up & Facts of Life > Family Life > New Experiences
column9: A charming fractured fairy-tale about how the road to success is often paved with mistakes and the most important thing is to keep trying. Once upon a time, there were three hopeful fairy-tale characters: Wolfred, Zinderella, and the Non-Evil Queen. Already rejected from classic fairy-tales, a happily-ever-after for these three seems a world away. So, the trio is headed to the School of Failure. Once there, they discover that with patience and persistence, mistakes can also lead to the perfect storybook ending. From author Rosie J. Pova and illustrator Monika Filipina comes a sweet and sassy fractured fairy-tale about beloved characters who don't make the final cut to be in a famous story but still find their starring roles. A perfect read for fans of THE BOOK OF MISTAKES , THE TRUE STORY OF THE THREE LITTLE PIGS , or anyone who needs a reminder that the road to success is often paved with mistakes, but that shouldn't stop us from pursuing our goals.
column28:
Review: ""Failing your way to fabulous." A delightful and refreshing take on failure that shows kids how imperfection is an expected and necessary part of success. The story highlights the importance of experimenting as a tool for discovering your true self. The detailed illustrations are immensely fun to pore over. A wonderful addition to any child's library." -Karen Yin, author of Whole Whale and So Not Ghoul "My kids (5 and 8) really enjoyed this book. My 8 year old especially wanted it read again and again. In a culture that is obsessed with achievement and perfection, THE SCHOOL OF FAILURE: A STORY ABOUT SUCCESS is a breath of fresh air. I love the book's message that mistakes don't have to be bad or the end of the world - instead, they can be stepping stones for learning and growth that lead us further along the path of who we are meant to be. The book shares this message in a gentle and humorous fashion that appeals to children and reminds them that they don't have to be afraid of mistakes or failure." --Lindsay B. "A charming, fractured, picture book fairy-tale about the road to success often being paved with mistakes, but that it shouldn't stop us from pursuing our goals and the most important thing is to keep trying." —Midwest Book Review

Pova is an award-winning, multi-published children's book author, writing instructor, and creativity coach whose life's work is to inspire children to be bold, take chances, and chase their dreams. A charming fractured fairy-tale about how the road to success is often paved with mistakes and the most important thing is to keep trying.

Once upon a time, there were three hopeful fairy-tale characters: Wolfred, Zinderella, and the Non-Evil Queen. Already rejected from classic fairy-tales, a happily-ever-after for these three seems a world away. So, the trio is headed to the School of Failure. See what lessons they'll learn there as we read together!

column9: “LeJeune has crafted a pleasing story about a Cajun boy, a mud snowman, and religious faith suitable for young readers. His text is simple and easy-to-read. Words with cultural value are shown in bold and compiled in a “Cajun glossary.” The beautiful artwork conveys the feel of Christmas in semitropical south Louisiana. At the book’s core is a sincere lesson: “If you pray and wish in your heart, the hope inside of you can make the impossible happen.” ~ Dr. Shane K. Bernard, south Louisiana writer and historian. Author of The Cajuns: Americanization of a People Down in the Louisiana bayou, Christmas comes with more than presents under the tree. It comes with family, faith, laughter, and a touch of swamp magic. Join Remy, a curious Cajun boy, as he discovers the joy of holiday traditions and the unexpected friend who brings his Christmas holiday to life. With warmth, humor, and the rich spirit of Cajun culture, Remy and T’George: The Louisiana Snowman invites readers of all ages to celebrate the season through stories of heritage, imagination, and heart.

"Hello, Mr. Snowman," said George. "Is everything all right?" "Not really," the snowman said. I'm worried for the birds. Everything is covered in snow and they are hungry as they can't dig for worms. George jumped back into his yellow truck, shouting, "I have an idea. I think I can help. Wait for me here." He sped off home where he rushed straight to the kitchen and started baking. What are you up to? His mom called out. I'm making seed cookies for the birds. They are made from mashed bananas and sesame seeds. So the birds will love them. M tasty. I love them too. He giggled. Once outside, George loaded up his trailer with the basket of warm cookies and set off to find the snowman. "Thank you," said the snowman. "You have a heart full of kindness." laughed George. "And the birds have tummies full of seeds." The next morning, George woke early and looked out his window. "Oh, wow," he said. "The snow has all gone. The birds will be able to find their food again. But Mr. Snowman, the snowman was gone. But from that day on, whenever it snowed, George would take his seed cookies to feed the birds, so they never went hungry.
